methodological_rigor.justification: Comprehensive mechanistic study combining cellular assays (EV isolation, protein transfer validation), biochemical analyses (RIPK1 glycosylation status, phosphorylation), and in vivo models (syngeneic gallbladder cancer, optical imaging, histology). Pathway activation demonstrated through RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL axis. Therapeutic validation: RAGE antagonist + gemcitabine in model. However: limited in vivo sample sizes, no power calculation, mechanistic model may not reflect human PNI complexity.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Identifies EV-OGA/RIPK1-necroptosis/HMGB1-RAGE axis driving gallbladder cancer perineural invasion. PNI is strong prognostic marker and driver of poor outcomes. Proposed RAGE antagonist targeting provides therapeutic strategy. Translational path clear; clinical validation requires prospective studies.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe EV isolation protocols, protein transfer assays, in vivo models, and molecular characterization (RIPK1 glycosylation via mass spec, phosphorylation). Missing: ARRIVE checklist compliance, sample size justification for animal cohorts, complete statistical analyses, data availability statements for proteomic/RNA-seq data.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies extracellular vesicle-mediated OGA transfer as novel mechanism driving neuronal necroptosis in PNI context. RIPK1 glycosylation as regulatory mechanism in necroptosis pathway novel. HMGB1-RAGE feedback loop establishing tumor-neuron reciprocal signaling is mechanistically innovative.

writing_presentation.justification: Methods logically organized from EV isolation through mechanistic characterization to in vivo validation. Methods dense with biochemical detail (glycosylation mass spec, phosphorylation mapping). Results integration across cellular, biochemical, and in vivo levels effective.

key_strengths: Novel identification of EV-mediated OGA transfer triggering RIPK1-dependent neuronal necroptosis as PNI mechanism
RIPK1 glycosylation as regulatory switch enhancing phosphorylation and necroptotic activation is mechanistically innovative
Demonstration of tumor-neuron reciprocal signaling loop: cancer necroptosis → HMGB1 release → RAGE activation → accelerated PNI
Therapeutic targeting demonstrated: RAGE antagonist FPS-ZM1 synergy with gemcitabine in model
key_concerns: Limited in vivo model sizes; no prospective power calculation provided
Mechanistic model (syngeneic murine) may not fully recapitulate human gallbladder PNI biology
Clinical translation unvalidated: HMGB1-RAGE targeting not tested in human gallbladder cancer
RIPK1 glycosylation mechanism identified biochemically but functional necessity in neuronal necroptosis not formally proven
Data availability: no statement regarding proteomic mass spec data or RNA-seq repository deposition
chief_reviewer.rationale: Novel mechanistic pathway with clear translational potential. Preclinical validation supports tier 2 pending clinical investigation.
